clue.text: Insensitive Charlie, right fool!

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at a tactless man called Charlie, calling him a right fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass behaviour is grossly stupid and without sensitivity, so the words are near synonyms.

clue.text: By sea, kiln for drying in California

indicators.note: in means the kiln is placed inside the abbreviation for California

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops

explanation.surface: A drying kiln by the sea somewhere on the Californian shore.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast is the kiln used in Kent, England, to dry hops for brewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Coastal means situated on or near the shore, beside the ocean.

clue.text: Metro ride chap arranged to see Paris monument

indicators.note: arranged tells us the letters of these three words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A man takes the Paris Metro to go and see a landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: This triumphal arch stands at the top of the Champs-Elysees, a famous landmark of the French capital.

clue.text: Identity assumed for men, woman and me

parts.note: a stag party or night is for men only
Ena is a woman's name

explanation.surface: Someone adopts a disguise to pass among men, a woman and the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer's professional pseudonym is an assumed identity used instead of their real name.

clue.text: Worrier fired up seeing initially awkward situation

indicators.note: initially tells us to take the opening letter of each of the three words before it

parts.note: to be in a spot is to be in an awkward situation

explanation.surface: Someone anxious gets worked up on finding themselves in a tricky position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired up' reads as a phrase meaning agitated, but its two words simply give their first letters, F and U, with S from 'seeing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusspot is a person who frets over trivial details, a kind of worrier.

clue.text: Foster often wrong, grabbing maiden

indicators.note: grabbing means the rearranged letters seize and hold the maiden letter inside
wrong suggests the letters of often are put out of order

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A foster parent often gets it wrong while grabbing a young girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns OFTEN into FOENT; 'grabbing' puts M inside it. A maiden over in cricket is one where no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To foment trouble is to foster or stir it up: a synonym in the sense of encourage.

clue.text: Beastly home in West Yorkshire

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are found inside the words West Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An animal's dwelling somewhere in West Yorkshire, an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigsty is a home for a beast, a pig; 'beastly' is used playfully for animal.

clue.text: Newly evidenced, paid? This at conflict's end?

indicators.note: newly means the letters of these words are made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: A question about money shown to be paid out once a war is over.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names money freed up when defence spending falls after a war ends.

clue.text: Colour that is not trendy at first

indicators.note: at first tells us to take the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A shade of paint that was unfashionable when it first appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: A tint is a shade or hue, a variety of colour.

clue.text: Be enthusiastic about account, one saying little about island

indicators.note: about means the following word for a quiet person goes around the island letter

parts.note: a clam is a person who says little, as in 'clam up'

explanation.surface: Instructions to praise a story told by a taciturn islander, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To acclaim something is to praise it publicly and enthusiastically, so it is a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Long twelvemonth at end of campaign

parts.note: a twelvemonth is an old word for a year

indicators.note: at end of tells us to take only the final letter of the word campaign

explanation.surface: A politician longs for a whole year after the campaign finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the twelvemonth, but it is the verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn for it: the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Soothing word with the head of News, immediately

parts.note: 'there, there' is said to soothe someone upset
and can mean with, joining things together

indicators.note: head of tells us to take the first letter of the word News

explanation.surface: A comforting word from the editor-in-chief of a news outlet, given straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the spot, without delay, is doing it at once: an idiom for straight away.

clue.text: Pungency of a new drink girl imbibes

indicators.note: imbibes means the girl's name takes the other pieces inside, as if drinking them

parts.note: Tess is a girl's name
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A girl tries a new drink with a sharp, strong taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns describe a sharp, strong flavour or smell: they are synonyms.

clue.text: A trial — faulty lasso

indicators.note: faulty suggests the letters of 'A trial' are broken and need reassembling

explanation.surface: A trial that went wrong, perhaps of a cowboy's rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a long rope with a running noose, used by cowboys: the same thing as a lasso.

clue.text: Finish repair work Monsieur's left

indicators.note: has left, meaning Monsieur departs and his letter is taken out

parts.note: mending is the work of repairing
M is the abbreviation for the French title Monsieur

explanation.surface: A Frenchman has walked out, so the repair job must be wrapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monsieur's left' reads as possessive but is 'Monsieur has left': drop M.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is the conclusion or close of something, a synonym for a finish.

clue.text: Lively good popular gallery, all going

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: going means the word all leaves, taken out of the gallery

parts.note: taken as the word itself, gallery
taken as written

explanation.surface: A well-liked gallery is buzzing, with everyone heading there.
explanation.definitionFit: Gingery can mean spirited or full of energy, like ginger's sharp kick, hence lively.

clue.text: Barrel-maker in company work, retro, off and on

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: off and on means take every other letter of the word retro

explanation.surface: A cask maker at a firm whose old-fashioned work comes and goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooper is a craftsman who makes and repairs barrels and casks.

clue.text: Central European with job — good place to start

parts.note: a Pole comes from Poland, in central Europe
a position is a job or post

explanation.surface: A worker from central Europe lands a job that is a good starting point for a career.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing, the front spot on the starting grid is the best place from which to begin a race.

clue.text: Done, and fast, extremely skilful

indicators.note: extremely tells us to take the outermost letters of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Something done quickly and with great skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Deft means neatly skilful and quick in movement, a synonym.

clue.text: Vain attempt you keep hidden

indicators.note: the words attempt you keep the letters concealed within them

explanation.surface: A futile effort that you should keep secret.
explanation.definitionFit: An empty threat or gesture is a vain one: without substance or effect.

clue.text: Animal talk

definitions.meaning: to chatter or prattle on at length

explanation.surface: Animal talk
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a Himalayan ox and an informal verb meaning to chatter.

clue.text: Go in advance of gym class, crossing playground with journalist

indicators.note: crossing means the gym class letters span the playground and journalist pieces, sitting either side of them

parts.note: PE is physical education, a school gym class
a rec is a recreation ground, a playground
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Pupils are told to arrive ahead of a PE lesson, walking across the playground with a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede is to come or go before something in time or order.

clue.text: He makes long journey finally short — about kilometre forward and back?

indicators.note: finally tells us to take the last letter of the word short

parts.note: RE is Latin-derived crossword shorthand for about, regarding
K is the abbreviation for kilometre

indicators.note: the pair for about and kilometre is written once forwards, then again backwards

explanation.surface: A walker's long trek ends up short, going a kilometre out and back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward and back' asks for RE K followed by its reversal KER, giving REKKER after T.
explanation.definitionFit: A trekker is a person who goes on a long, arduous journey, usually on foot.

clue.text: Son nervous describing grasses

parts.note: edgy means tense or nervous

explanation.surface: A jittery boy writes about meadow grasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant, so the adjective formed from it describes ground full of such grasses.
